glossary/terms.json.orbit: The closed path a body follows around another under gravity — an ellipse in the simplest case.
glossary/terms.json.trajectory: The path a spacecraft follows through space, open or closed — for example the arc from Earth to Mars.
glossary/terms.json.inclination: The tilt of an orbit's plane against a reference plane, such as Earth's equator or the ecliptic, in degrees.
glossary/terms.json.rendezvous: Bringing two spacecraft to the same place at the same speed so that they fly together — usually the step before docking.
glossary/terms.json.docking: Joining two spacecraft mechanically so that crew or cargo can pass between them.
glossary/terms.json.gravity assist: Using a close pass of a planet to change a spacecraft's speed and direction without spending propellant.
glossary/terms.json.delta-v: Change in velocity, written Δv: how much a spacecraft can change its motion, the currency of every mission plan, in km/s.
glossary/terms.json.apogee: The point of an orbit around Earth that is farthest from Earth.
glossary/terms.json.perigee: The point of an orbit around Earth that is closest to Earth.
glossary/terms.json.burn: A period of firing a rocket engine to change a spacecraft's velocity.
glossary/terms.json.stage: A section of a rocket with its own engines and propellant, dropped when its propellant is used up.
glossary/terms.json.propellant: What a rocket engine uses up to make thrust: usually a fuel and an oxidizer together.
glossary/terms.json.payload: What a rocket carries for the mission: satellites, a crewed spacecraft, cargo or instruments.
glossary/terms.json.thrust: The force a rocket engine produces to push the vehicle forward, measured in newtons.
glossary/terms.json.booster: A rocket that provides thrust at launch: a first stage, or a strap-on rocket at the side of the core.
glossary/terms.json.specific impulse: How efficiently an engine uses its propellant, in seconds: the higher it is, the more Δv from the same propellant.
glossary/terms.json.flyby: A close pass by a planet, moon or other body without going into orbit around it or landing.
glossary/terms.json.orbit insertion: The engine burn that slows a spacecraft enough to be captured into orbit around its destination.
glossary/terms.json.entry: A spacecraft's passage into a planet's atmosphere, where drag and heating slow it down.
glossary/terms.json.descent: The way down to a surface, from orbit or from the atmosphere to touchdown.
